newsitem.title: USA: "Prairie Potholes" new conservation priority area.
newsitem.headline: "Prairie Potholes" new conservation priority area.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman announced Tuesday the Prairie Pothole Region of the upper Great Plains Region -- one of the nation's most important waterfowl nesting areas -- will be added to the national conservation priority areas for the Conservation Reserve Programme (CRP).
The Agriculture Department is finalising new rules for the CRP and Glickman told Reuters earlier Tuesday that the new regulations will likely be unveiled next week.

Created in 1985, the reserve programme pays farmers an annual rent for taking fragile land out of production for 10 years. About 36.4 million acres were enrolled in the reserve, making it the largest long-term U.S. land retirement programme ever.

While some conservations have fretted that the new rules could be too lax, some lawmakers have feared a bias against the Plains states. The move by the Agriculture Department to include the Plains-based Prairie Potholes Region in CRP's priority area was seen partially as a move to placate those lawmakers, especially Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota.

Cropland located within a conservation priority area is most likely to be enrolled in the CRP, but owners of that land still have to bid to be in the programme and only those areas that are determined to provide siginificant environmental benefit will be accepted.
The Long Island Sound, Chesapeake Bay, and Great Lakes Regions have already been designated as national conservation priority areas in past CRP's.

To be classified as a conservation priority area, it must be determined that retiring agricultural lands in these specific areas offers the potential for significant water quality and wildlife habitat benefits.

Glickman said that the Prairie Potholes provide a prime waterfowl nesting area, and that CRP enrollment in this area has contributed to "remarkable wildlife benefits in that area and in many other regions of the nation."

"This year's waterfowl population was the highest since the early 1970's," said Glickman. "Much of this increase has been attributed to the prime waterfowl nesting area provided by CRP acreage in the Prairie Pothole Region."
